name: First Financial Bankshares, Inc.
reason: Conservatively run Texas community bank with low-cost deposit franchise, ~14% avg ROE, 8.7% 10y EPS CAGR with only ~1%/yr share growth and no leveraged M&A; NIM is rate-sensitive (2023 EPS -14%) and FY2-3 consensus only ~5-6%, so growth route needs verification.

name: WesBanco, Inc.
reason: Acquisition-driven regional bank: shares up 9.3%/yr over 10y versus only 3.8% EPS CAGR and ~6.9% avg ROE - ordinary franchise with no specialness.

name: ConocoPhillips
reason: E&P earnings set by oil and gas prices (EPS swung from -2.66 to 13.52 over the decade; 2025 EPS 0.46x 10y peak) - unforecastable commodity exposure.

name: Cullen/Frost Bankers, Inc.
reason: Disciplined Texas bank with a top-tier low-cost deposit/service franchise growing organically (de novo branches, zero acquisitions, flat share count), 8.8% 10y / 14.2% 5y EPS CAGR and ~12.8% ROE; EPS at 10y peak on rates, so rate sensitivity must be stress-tested.

name: DaVita, Inc.
reason: EPS growth (10.9% CAGR) came almost entirely from buybacks (shares -9.9%/yr) on flat revenue with net debt/EBITDA 4.5x, and dialysis economics hinge on government reimbursement and GLP-1/CKD-therapy volume risk.

name: Spire Inc.
reason: Regulated gas utility with only 3.4% 10y EPS CAGR, net debt/EBITDA 6.4x and long-run gas-electrification risk - no route to 7% growth.

name: Exelon Corp.
reason: Regulated T&D utility with 4.5% 10y EPS CAGR, negative FCF and net debt/EBITDA 5.6x; data-center load helps rate base but EPS growth remains regulated at ~5-7% - ordinary, not special.

name: Teradata Corp.
reason: Legacy on-prem data warehouse losing share to cloud-native rivals (revenue -4.1%/yr over 10y); EPS growth is buyback-driven and AI/cloud disintermediation threat is live.

name: CVR Energy, Inc.
reason: Refiner/fertilizer earnings driven by crack spreads and nitrogen prices (EPS from 6.04 in 2022 to -1.22 in 2025) - commodity-set and unforecastable.

name: Chimera Investment Corp.
reason: Mortgage REIT whose earnings depend on rate and credit spreads; EPS fell from 7.11 to 1.68 over 10y (-13.4%/yr) - fails the rate/credit-cycle test.

name: Walker & Dunlop, Inc.
reason: Commercial real estate lending/brokerage tied to transaction volumes and rates; EPS down from 8.15 (2021) to 1.64 (2025), 0.2x 10y peak - capital-markets cyclicality.

name: Booz Allen Hamilton Holding Corp.
reason: Strong record (14.7% 10y EPS CAGR, 8/10 growth years) but essentially a single customer (US government) facing civil-spending cuts and procurement disruption plus AI pressure on consulting labor models; FY1 consensus -2.5% and margin at 91st pctile.

name: Fortune Brands Innovations, Inc.
reason: Good brands (Moen, Master Lock) but housing/R&R-cyclical with flat 10y revenue (-0.3%/yr), 5y EPS CAGR 0.2%, acquisition spend ~54% of FCF and FY1 consensus -7.5% - no clear route to 7%.

name: Mueller Water Products, Inc.
reason: Oligopoly hydrant/valve franchise with secular water-infrastructure demand, but revenue grew only 2.1%/yr and EPS is at its 10y peak with EBIT margin at a 10y high (18.8% vs 13.4% avg) after a sharp 2024-25 run-up, so normalized earnings power is uncertain.

name: PennyMac Mortgage Investment Trust
reason: Mortgage REIT with earnings driven by rates, MSR valuations and credit (EPS -1.25 in 2022, 0.99 in 2025), net debt/EBITDA 13.5x - fails the rate/credit-cycle and balance-sheet tests.

name: Graphic Packaging Holding Co.
reason: Growth came from acquisitions and leverage (acq spend 6.0x FCF over 10y, net debt/EBITDA 4.0x) and EPS has fallen to 0.62x its 2023 peak with FY1 consensus -62% amid paperboard overcapacity.

name: Royalty Pharma Plc
reason: Royalty model is attractive but earnings depend on patent-cliff timing of a few blockbusters (Imbruvica, Januvia, Tysabri, Promacta rolling off) and on continuous deal-making at uncertain returns, with net debt/EBITDA 5.3x and a very large GAAP vs adjusted gap.

name: EnerSys
reason: Industrial battery maker whose EPS jump (5.34 to 10.56 since 2022) is heavily aided by IRA 45X manufacturing credits (adj vs GAAP gap ~27%) subject to policy risk, with margins at 91st pctile and cyclical forklift/telecom demand.

name: AECOM
reason: Recently transformed into asset-light design/consulting (exited construction) with EPS 19.6% 5y CAGR and margin at a 10y high (6.6%), but revenue shrank 1.1%/yr, GAAP vs adjusted gap ~224% and AI may pressure engineering-design labor billing.

name: Cheniere Energy Partners LP
reason: Largely contracted LNG cash flows, but EPS is 0.74x its 2023 peak with consensus -7%/-9% for FY1-FY2, net debt/EBITDA 3.4x and residual spot-margin exposure - no route to 7% growth.
